source_text.body:
Build a multi-agent system on AWS
The author built a multi-agent system on AWS as the final project of Udacity's AWS Agent Engineer Nanodegree.
·
Nov 25, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
Using Strands Agents and Bedrock AgentCore, the author built a fictional NovaMart support system. An Orchestrator routed requests to Inventory, Policy, Refund and Communication agents, saving each result to a shared DynamoDB WorkflowState with optimistic locking and up to three retries. The Policy Agent queried three Knowledge Bases in parallel with ThreadPoolExecutor.
How it went
The full test suite scored 120/120. One NameError from a missing retrievers dictionary came up during testing and was fixed. The author does not report time savings from the parallel retrieval.
Worth knowing
The Udacity starter environment already supplied the DynamoDB tables, S3 resources, IAM role and log group. The author cleaned up AWS resources afterward to avoid charges.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Help me build a small multi-agent system on AWS for [describe the task, e.g. triaging customer support emails]. Start by proposing an architecture with one coordinator agent and [number] specialist agents, and tell me which AWS services each would use. Then scaffold the code in this folder, add a README with deploy steps, and stop once I can run one end-to-end test locally. Pause and show me the plan before you create or change anything in my AWS account.
Original source: https://dev.to/hemapriya_kanagala/i-built-my-first-multi-agent-system-on-aws-and-it-was-easier-than-i-expected-58c2
